title: Rose of Lima (1586–1617)
hook: a young woman in a garden hut in Lima, remembered as the first canonized saint of the Americas

segments.voice: Yesterday, Matteo Ricci in a scholar's robe, and the long word inculturation. Your line was friendship first. Did you ask anyone a real question about their world? Day eight hundred fifty-eight.

At the back of a family garden in Lima, in Peru, there's a hut with barely room for one person. Inside, a young woman sews. Her needlework and the flowers she grows help keep her family fed. Some days the door opens onto a different job: sick and hungry people from the city, whom she brings into a room of her parents' house and nurses herself. She never enters a convent. She never travels. And yet the Church remembers her as the first person from the Americas to be named a saint. Her baptismal name was Isabel. In time she was called Rose.
screen: `A HUT IN A GARDEN.` → `NEEDLEWORK AND FLOWERS.` → `THE SICK IN HER PARENTS' HOUSE.`

segments.voice: Tradition says the name Rose came from a servant who saw her as a baby and thought her face looked like a rose. She kept it. First, a life at home. Rose wanted a life given to God, but she did not join an enclosed convent. She became a Dominican tertiary: a laywoman who follows the spirituality of the Dominicans while living in the world. Her cloister was a hut in her family's garden. Second, the work of her hands. She sewed and sold flowers to help her family, and she took the poor and sick into her parents' house and nursed them herself. Third, the hard part, and it should be told honestly. Rose practiced severe penances: fasting, sleeping on hard boards, wearing things meant to hurt. Her biographers wrote about these as heroic. Some Catholics today read them more carefully, as signs of a fierce love that should not be copied, and the Church does not ask anyone to imitate them. Fourth, the cross at the center. Rose's spirituality kept returning to the suffering Christ. Paul put it in one line, in the Douay-Rheims: "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." She belonged to a city full of new wealth and old wounds, the city of conquerors and of the conquered. When the Church later named her a saint, the Americas had their first. Lima still keeps her feast as its own.
screen: `A ROSE, NAMED BY A SERVANT.` · `A TERTIARY IN A GARDEN HUT.` · `FLOWERS, NEEDLEWORK, THE SICK.` · `PENANCES: TOLD HONESTLY.` · then, large: `SAVE IN THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for Latin America, or hold it in mind. Settle, and breathe. Picture a map, from Mexico down to the far south. Let a few places rise: a city you've heard of, a country in the news, a family you know who comes from there. Rest on one. If you pray, you can ask Rose of Lima to pray for that place, or say a Hail Mary for its people. If you don't pray, simply hold them, the sick and the poor especially, the ones Rose brought into her parents' house. The bell holds the time.
Dominican tertiary. A laywoman who follows the spirituality of the Dominicans while living in the world, the life Rose of Lima chose instead of an enclosed convent.

Your line: first of the americas. Today, when news from Latin America reaches you, let it be people before it is a headline, and name one of them, even just a city, in your heart. Day eight hundred fifty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholics in Peru and across Latin America keep the feast of Saint Rose of Lima, often with processions, and some Dominican laypeople look to her as a model of holiness lived outside a convent.
